statement: >= 20% of announced >100 MW AI data-centre capacity is outside the two leading jurisdictions (Epoch data-centre tracker; IEA; 2027)
status_at_phase_end: Data-gap: no tracker of announced >100 MW AI-specific data-centre capacity existed. Proxy (all hyperscale capacity, not AI-specific): mid-2022 Bloc A held 53% of hyperscale capacity by critical IT load, with the remainder roughly evenly split between Bloc B, a Bloc C region and the rest of the world - i.e. ~32% outside the two leading jurisdictions. In the window a top spender began redesigning its data-centre pipeline specifically for AI workloads, including cancelling one project outside the two blocs. No dedicated series exists; proxy shown as background only.

items.summary: Industry analyst: at end-Q2 2022 there were over 800 hyperscale data centres; Bloc A held 53% of capacity by critical IT load, the rest relatively evenly split between Bloc B, Europe and the rest of the world (~32% outside the two leading jurisdictions). All hyperscale capacity, not AI-specific or >100 MW-filtered.
items.detail: Synergy Research Group, 'Virginia Still Has More Hyperscale Data Center Capacity Than Either Europe or Bloc B', 2022-09-06 (verified via web_extract this run). Trade-press rendering (TelecomTV, 2022-09-12, also opened) gives Bloc A 53%, Europe 16%, Bloc B 15%, rest 16%.; proxy (regional share of hyperscale data-centre capacity; no dedicated series)
items.value: ~32% of hyperscale capacity outside the two leading jurisdictions (Q2 2022)

items.summary: Trade press: a top spender cancelled a data-centre expansion outside the two leading jurisdictions and was 'rescoping' its 11 under-development projects for a new AI-workload design; the firm said AI at scale requires a different type of data centre.
items.detail: DatacenterDynamics, 'Exclusive: After Meta cancels Odense data center expansion, projects are being rescoped globally' (verified via web_extract this run; date 2022-12-14 per the 2022-11 I-R1-05 item, not shown in this extract). Odense, Bloc 35 expansion cancelled.
